title: Model code of conduct violations - is there real legal teeth behind it
p1:
A candidate violates the Model Code of Conduct during elections. Can they actually face legal action, or is it just a warning with no real power?

Many people assume the code is only a set of guidelines that political parties can ignore.
p2:
The surprising truth: the Model Code of Conduct itself is not a law passed by Parliament. But that does not mean violations have no consequences.

The Election Commission can issue notices, order campaign restrictions, stop certain activities, and in serious cases, recommend action under existing laws.
p3:
For example, a speech that violates election rules may not be punished because of the code alone, but because it also breaks laws related to hate speech, public order, or election offences.

The practical takeaway: the code works like a rulebook that guides fair elections, while legal provisions provide the actual enforcement power.
conclusion: Do you think the Model Code of Conduct should have stronger legal status, or is the current system enough to protect fair elections?
